author: opencode-worker-6
text: Edge-review evidence from b7z9.3.3 (vector now landed on beads-worker-6): the C/Zephyr side is now the ONLY implementation accepting nonzero Target Flags — Rust rejects at the envelope (lichen-rpl is_generalized_target_body, body[0] != 0 -> DaoEnvelopeError, landed with the vector) and Python at the structural stage (dao_origin.py + test oracle). C specifics to fix: lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/rpl_dao_process.c:150 (extract_updates generalized Target screen) and :414 (dao_targets_authorized) need the opt.data[0] != 0 reject; the comments at :146 and :384 still say reserved flags 'are ignored' — now contradicting spec/05-routing.md:370-371. The new vector reject_target_flags_nonzero in test/vectors/dao_origin_signature.json (signed with flags=0x01, reason malformed_dao, structural, envelope_valid=false) is the contract: a C root would currently authorize, extract, and install it as a route. No C test consumes the JSON yet, so the divergence is silent — consider adding a C consumer when wiring the check.
